summary: Same Enchantments in an item components crashes the game
description: when you have 2 enchantments "sharpness" and "minecraft:sharpness" in the new components this will crash the game 1. give s diamond_sword[enchantments {levels:{sharpness:10,"sharpness":10}}] 2. give s diamond_sword[enchantments {levels:{sharpness:10,"minecraft:sharpness":10}}] the second one will crash the game, but the first one doesnt.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. Use the command `/give @p diamond_sword[enchantments:{levels:{sharpness:10,"sharpness":10}}]` to give yourself a diamond sword with duplicate "sharpness" enchantments.
4. Observe that the game does not crash after receiving this item.
5. Use the command `/give @p diamond_sword[enchantments:{levels:{sharpness:10,"minecraft:sharpness":10}}]` to give yourself another diamond sword with both "sharpness" and "minecraft:sharpness" enchantments.
6. Observe that the game crashes after receiving this item.
Observed Behavior: When an item has duplicate enchantments such as "sharpness" and "minecraft:sharpness," it causes the game to crash under specific conditions. For example, using the command `/give s diamond_sword[enchantments {levels:{sharpness:10,"sharpness":10}}]` does not cause a crash because both enchantments are named identically as "sharpness." However, when the command is modified to include `minecraft:sharpness` with the same level, such as `/give s diamond_sword[enchantments {levels:{sharpness:10,"minecraft:sharpness":10}}]`, it results in a game crash. This issue arises due to how the game processes and differentiates between enchantment names, leading to an unexpected conflict when both "sharpness" and "minecraft:sharpness" are present simultaneously on the same item.
Expected Behavior: When an item has duplicate enchantments like "sharpness" and "minecraft:sharpness," the game should not crash. Instead, it should handle these duplicates gracefully by either merging them into a single valid enchantment or ignoring the redundant one. Both commands should execute without crashing, resulting in a diamond sword with the appropriate sharpness levels applied.
